title: Divine testimony from Scripture's implanted efficacy and the Spirit's inward work; against Miletus on Aesop
pass_a_gloss: 7. But this divine testimony is both from that efficacy which we have said was so divinely implanted in scripture that its authority does not depend through itself from proofs sought elsewhere, and from the interior operation of the Holy Spirit in the heart of the reader — which is called the earnest and seal given by God to the faithful, and the spirit of judgment and of burning, Isa. 4:4, and fire Matt. 3:11. Therefore Vitus Miletus of Gmünd, a pontifical man, acts the part of the profane and atheist, not of a Christian to whom the force of scripture is known, when he says: We say that if you take away the authority of the church, sacred scripture will not be worth even as much as the fables of Aesop.
pass_b_english: This divine testimony is both from the efficacy so divinely implanted in Scripture that its authority does not of itself depend on proofs sought elsewhere, and from the Holy Spirit's inward operation in the reader's heart. That operation, though it cannot alone convince others, vehemently confirms the one who already reads and believes — called the earnest and seal given to believers, the spirit of judgment and of burning ([[Isaiah 4:4 >> Bible:Isaiah 4:4]]), and fire ([[Matthew 3:11 >> Bible:Matthew 3:11]]).

Those who by Aph. VII's monitory and motive arguments have already acknowledged the Christian religion as more probable cannot but admit this testimony's divinity. Therefore Vitus Miletus of Gmünd, a papal man, acts the atheist, not the Christian who knows Scripture's force, when he says: take away the Church's authority and Sacred Scripture will not even be worth Aesop's fables — take away the Church's infallible authority and tradition, and Scripture will have no certainty among humans.
source_text: Testimonium divinum ab efficacia indita & interiore Spiritus operatione (arrhabo, σφραγίς, Esa. 4.4, Matth. 3.11). Contra Vitum Miletum Gamundianum, qui scripturam sine Ecclesiae authoritate Aesopi fabulis aequiparat.
